artboards.title: AstroTalk Kundli — a real API mapped

annotations.text:
One screen per connector, no tabs.

Seven fields, a static macro list and a deployment fact used to be five tabs. Everything is on screen at once, so nothing is closed — which is what "why are other sections closed?" was actually asking for.

Navigation: the sidebar, and an action's tabs. Two rows of tabs are now impossible.

Tabs survive in exactly one place: inside an action, where Params / Headers / Body really are alternative views of one request.

Every table is the same five columns: Key · Type · Source · Description · Required. No enable/disable checkbox — Meta has no disabled parameter, so Required is the only real one.

Send and Response — the correction that matters.

I had been saying a test was impossible because Meta makes the call at runtime. Wrong: for VERIFICATION our own server can make it and show you the response. Without that you configure blind and find out from a customer.

What this needs, and what it costs:
• the credential typed for the test, held for that one request, never stored
• an SSRF guard — the server must refuse private ranges, localhost and 169.254.169.254, with a timeout and a response cap
• honesty: our egress is not Meta's, so a request that passes here can still be refused there by an IP allowlist

Auth is two rows of the connector's property table, and the credentials are a table.

The In column (Header / Query / Body) is the whole of gap G1: Meta accepts credentials in all three and we only ever built headers, so every ?api_key= API was unconfigurable.

An action's Auth tab reports what it inherits and links here — Meta ignores a per-tool override, so offering one would lie.

The founder's question: "if I have to map fields of the body and all with the agent how do I give the description?"

Answer, from mapping his API: the description is not documentation, it is the contract. Meta records required-ness only for TOP-LEVEL body fields, and this API nests everything under one — so day, month, year, lat and lon are all genuinely required and none of them can be marked required. There is no min, no max, no pattern either.

So the description carries the range, the unit, the format and the word required, in words. lat wants decimal degrees and will not geocode a place name; hour wants 0 for midnight, never 24.

And a failed call returns HTTP 200 with status:failed — so the ACTION's description, not a field's, has to tell the agent to read status before trusting the body.

Copy standard, visible rather than described: nouns, not sentences. Actions. Agents. Source. Agent. Fixed. Up to date. JSON only.

Gone: "What it can do", "Who fills this in", "Agent fills this in", "built from its fields", "Still needed: Name, Description (Docs tab)".

Macros read as {{customer_phone}} — standard token style, mapped to Meta's constant on the way out, so nobody reads a Meta constant.
